regeln: Align imagery with specific business concepts like market traps, refusals, or competition; avoid generic workshop scenes or visual puns that lack context.
Conclude scripts with a tight, driven payoff or final insight rather than repeating or recapping earlier narrative beats.
Preserve the signature painted open-world-game style and consistent presenter identities: Fedora for Business, Leather Jacket for AI.
Use genuine source-backed evidence and real tool interfaces; never use stock or illustrations as substitutes for real results.
Begin with a high-stakes narrative hook presenting a core conflict or transformation within the first three seconds.
Show main imagery prominently in the frame; avoid tiny photos, empty spaces, or unrelated background-only frames.
Deliver on title promises by explaining all specific terms, nicknames, or payoffs in both the script and the visuals.
Focus tool explanations on practical human tasks and concrete limits rather than technical benchmarks or architecture tags.
Include mandatory spoken like, share, and save calls at their designated format-specific positions.
Never override source-supported facts, limits, or approved voices with speculation or unobserved causes.
Maintain format-specific pacing: do not impose Short-video speed on long videos or long-video chapter pacing on Shorts.
Treat reviewer feedback as provisional data to improve habits; phrase lessons conditionally and avoid over-generalizing single defects.
